WITH sql_db AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = s.file_id
  WHERE s.name = 'SQLDatabase' AND s.kind = 'class' AND f.module = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py'
),
connectors AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT cb.class_symbol_id
  FROM code.class_bases cb
  JOIN sql_db b ON b.symbol_id = cb.base_symbol_id
  JOIN code.symbols cs ON cs.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id
  JOIN code.files cf ON cf.file_id = cs.file_id
  WHERE NOT cf.is_test
    AND cf.module NOT LIKE '%/tests/%'
    AND cf.module NOT LIKE 'tests/%'
),
sql_methods AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.name
  FROM code.symbols s
  JOIN sql_db b ON b.symbol_id = s.symbol_id
  WHERE s.kind = 'method'
)
SELECT DISTINCT c.class_symbol_id, m.name AS method_name
FROM connectors c
JOIN code.symbols m ON m.symbol_id = c.class_symbol_id
WHERE m.kind = 'method'
  AND m.name NOT LIKE '\_%' ESCAPE '\'
  AND m.name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM sql_methods)
ORDER BY c.class_symbol_id, m.name

request:
The production database connectors are the classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase (defined in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py), excluding any class defined in test code (every file under a tests/ folder counts as test code). For each such connector class, which public methods does the class define in its own body that SQLDatabase itself does not define? A method is public when its name does not start with an underscore (so __init__ and other dunder methods are excluded); anything written with def directly in the class body counts as a method, including properties and context-manager methods. Methods inherited without being redefined do not count. Return one row per (connector class symbol ID, method name).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), method_name (string).
explanation: Finds SQLDatabase's symbol, then all classes that directly subclass it via class_bases, excluding classes in test files. For each connector class, it selects methods defined in that class body whose names don't start with an underscore and that SQLDatabase does not itself define, returning one row per class/method pair.

    AND cf.module NOT LIKE '%/tests/%'

sql_methods AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.name

  JOIN sql_db b ON b.symbol_id = s.symbol_id

SELECT DISTINCT c.class_symbol_id, m.name AS method_name
